Subject: Recap & next steps — POC prompt/logs request and evaluation roadmap

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed concrete path for the trial so we can get your team unblocked: 

- Scope we discussed: evaluate Redwood Inference for Celerity’s automated summarization and support-assist flows (customer chat logs -> one-paragraph summaries + suggested next actions).
- What we need from you: a) a de-identified prompt/log sample (500–2,000 conversational turns or ~10k–50k tokens) that represents the heavy tails, b) a short spec of expected labels (summary length, redaction rules), and c) any compliance constraints (retention, sharing redaction salt).

Proposed success criteria (draft):
- Automated summary quality: 85% pass rate on rubric-derived automated checks (semantic overlap + key-entity coverage).
- Human acceptability: >=90% of sampled summaries rated usable by your CS reviewers (N=200 blind eval).
- Operational: p50 generation latency <= 350ms for 512 tokens; no more than 1% generation errors at p95.

Evaluation plan (high level):
- You deliver prompt/log bundle (JSONL) and label spec by Jan 19.
- Redwood runs an initial automated eval (synthetic metrics, EM/ROUGE-ish proxies) within 5 business days.
- Hand off ~200 samples for human review (we can coordinate panel or Celerity reviewers).

Ownership:
- Celerity: provide sample bundle + spec, internal reviewer pool, legal signoff for PII handling.
- Redwood: run baseline eval, produce report, and support a 60-minute alignment call with results.

Attachments: I’m including the evaluation template and a short prompt transfer checklist to make the handoff easier.

Next steps: Can you confirm if Jan 19 works to deliver the sample bundle and whether we should route transfer via S3 presigned links or your secure Share? Once we have that, I’ll lock the timeline and book the results review on Jan 26.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this going.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Hi Sam —

Thanks for the sample and the transfer preference. A few technical clarifications to make the evaluation smooth: 

1) Preferred payload format: JSONL where each line is an object with fields: id, conversation (array of turns with speaker tags), metadata (optional), and target_summary (when available). Example schema is in prompt-transfer-instructions.pdf.

2) Token budgeting: for sampling we prefer keeping most examples <= 2,048 tokens but can handle longer tails — please flag any >8k tokens.

3) PII/anonymization: your approach sounds good. If you can provide an anonymization map (simple lookup of account_id -> masked token) we can run internal checks without needing raw identifiers. If legal insists on no mapping transfer, we can operate with fully redacted data but may need longer human eval to compensate.

4) Secure transfer: S3 presigned is fine. For the presigned object please set server-side encryption (AES256) and provide a short TTL (>72h). If you prefer Redwood-managed ingestion, we can provide a one-time upload endpoint.

5) Evaluation specifics we’ll run on receipt: automated semantic-overlap scoring (embedding-based), entity coverage checks, and a heuristic for hallucination triggers. After automated pass we’ll select 200 cases for blind human review. Acceptance thresholds (draft): 85% automated pass, >=90% human usable. If you want more conservative thresholds, flag now.

Owners (confirmed):
- Celerity: Sam (data), Legal (policy), CS reviewers (human eval).
- Redwood: Dev Patel (engineer lead for eval), Jasmine Liu (commercial owner), Eng Ops for upload.

I’ve attached a filled eval-template (poc-eval-template.xlsx) with fields we’ll populate after the first run.

If all that looks good we’ll expect the presigned link and the full bundle on Jan 19 and will schedule the automated run for Jan 20–22, with a results review call Jan 26.

Cheers,
Dev
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
